t:
(a) Study.—The Commandant of the Coast Guard shall conduct a study to assess the current homeport arrangement of the Coast Guard polar icebreaker HEALY to determine whether an alternative arrangement would enhance the Coast Guard’s capabilities to carry out the recommendation to maintain dedicated, year-round icebreaker capability for the Arctic that was included in the report prepared by the National Academy of Sciences and entitled: “Polar Icebreaker Roles and U.S. Future Needs: A Preliminary Assessment (ISBN: 0–309–10069–0)”. 
    (b) Report.—Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commandant shall report the findings of the study to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to a National Academy of Sciences report brings outside experts into the process. That report already exists and is only cited as the source of a recommendation; the section does not require any new consultation with the Academy or anyone else outside government. The only actors are the Coast Guard Commandant, who conducts the study, and congressional committees, who receive the report, and all of them are inside the federal government.
fable.s: the Commandant shall report the findings of the study to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Commandant of the Coast Guard to conduct a study and report the findings to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: The Commandant shall report the findings of the study to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

opus.w: The Coast Guard does the study internally and reports the results to congressional committees. Both actors are inside the federal government. The National Academy of Sciences report is an existing document cited for its recommendation, not a consultation with outside experts before a decision (compare Example 5's reference to a past agreement). No comment period, hearing, advisory body, or outside consultation is required.
opus.s: the Commandant shall report the findings of the study to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section cites a report by the National Academy of Sciences, which is an outside expert body, and it also requires a formal report. That can look like outside participation. It isn't. The Academy's report already exists and is only cited as the source of a recommendation. No outside party is consulted on a future federal decision. The required report goes to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The study is also done entirely within the Coast Guard.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Coast Guard to conduct an internal study and report its findings to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities before making a decision.
qwen_chat.s: The Commandant of the Coast Guard shall conduct a study to assess the current homeport arrangement of the Coast Guard polar icebreaker HEALY... Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commandant shall report the findings of the study to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the study relies on a report from the National Academy of Sciences (an outside entity), implying consultation. However, the text only cites the report as the source of a recommendation the Coast Guard is assessing; it does not require the Coast Guard to consult with the Academy or any other outside party during the study or decision-making process. The only output mentioned is a report to Congress, which is an internal government action.
